analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts an automated AWS Migration Factory workflow. 1. Pre-migration discovery and continuous replication: On-premises servers send connection/utilization metadata to AWS Application Discovery Service and continuous block-level volume data to an EC2 Hot Replica staging instance via CloudEndure. The Migration Team populates target account metadata, IP, subnet, RTO/RPO, and tags into DynamoDB. 2. Automated Migration Execution: The Migration Team triggers execution via Slack, which calls the Migration Factory EC2 instance API. The Migration Factory queries App Discovery for TCP metadata, tells CloudEndure to stop replication, bakes an AMI from the hot replica, shares the encrypted AMI to the target account using DynamoDB metadata, and launches the final target EC2 instance with proper sizing and tagging in about 10 minutes.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Snapchat's backend pipeline running on AWS. 1. Mobile clients (iOS/Android) interact through an EKS-hosted Gateway. 2. For sending snaps, the Gateway routes media traffic to the Media service (EKS), which pushes media through CloudFront into S3 for storage, and consults the Friend Graph service to manage relationship contacts. 3. For messaging, the Gateway routes to the Messaging Connection Service (MCS) in EKS, which checks connection mappings in Amazon ElastiCache and pushes active notifications/messages directly to client devices (e.g. Android). 4. analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates a legacy web application modernization pattern for American Family Group (Main Street America). Independent insurance agents (UserCompanyAgent) access a single-page application (SPA) hosted in S3 and delivered via CloudFront. CloudFront routes API requests to API Gateway, which invokes a custom Lambda Authorizer to validate access. Validated requests are handled by a serverless Python Lambda function. For modernized functions, Lambda interacts directly with a regional DynamoDB table for user session caching across Availability Zones. For unmigrated legacy functions, the Python Lambda forwards calls to an EC2 instance running a Tomcat Java application, which processes and returns data back to Lambda.

graph.name: American Family Group Main Street America Application Modernization
graph.notes: Serverless application architecture showcasing strangler-fig migration pattern from legacy Tomcat EC2 to AWS Lambda and DynamoDB.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture details a pipeline for acquiring and processing drone imagery for Marathon Oil. Drones upload flight images to a 3rd Party Software system. A scheduled CloudWatch Event triggers AWS Step Functions, which orchestrates three Lambda functions: checking for new images via API, copying new image files from the 3rd Party system directly into an S3 bucket, and creating raster proxies stored in the On-Prem Database. Finally, the On-Prem Server uses AWS Storage Gateway to access and read the raster imagery directly from the S3 bucket.
